info.desc: Ultra is the ninth studio album by the English electronic music band Depeche Mode, released on 14 April 1997 by Mute Records. The album was the band's first since the departure of Alan Wilder, who had left the band in 1995 having become disillusioned with life in Depeche Mode. Wilder's departure and lead singer Dave Gahan's drug problems, which culminated in a near-fatal overdose, had caused many people to speculate that the band was finished. This is their first album as a trio since 1982's A Broken Frame. .

podcast.body: Demos for this album were sent to Dave Gahan by Martin Gore while Dave was still struggling with severe drug addiction. The song "Sister of Night" from this album was notably recorded while Dave was high on heroin, and he could not manage to get through the full song in one take. "The story is that the song's sister of night, one of the tracks from the 1997 ultra album, was recorded while Dave was high on heroin."

podcast.body: Released in the mid-90s, Ultra was recorded during a profoundly difficult and crucial period for Depeche Mode, following Alan Wilder's departure and amidst the severe personal struggles of Dave Gahan and Martin Gore. The album initially received mixed critical reviews, but its standing has significantly grown over the years, becoming a beloved work for many fans due to its intense emotional depth. It explores a more intimate sound, reflecting the members' personal challenges and their eventual journey toward recovery. "Es un disco que con los años ha ganado muchísimo carisma."

podcast.body: Ultra marked a significant shift in Depeche Mode's musical direction, benefiting from the departure of Alan Wilder, which allowed the band to open up to new sonic horizons. The album incorporated influences from genres like Trip Hop, Krautrock, and German industrial music, moving away from synthesizer-based structures towards more complex, computerized foundations. It also featured an extensive list of collaborating musicians, contributing to a more complex and musically rich sound that defined the band's post-Wilder era. "Tenemos influencias de muchas otras estilos de música que posiblemente no hubiese sido posible todavía con el álbum, como esas influencias del Trip Hub que era tan potente a la mitad de los 90."
